strategies.name: opening_range_breakout_close_entry
strategies.entry_summary: Define the 15-minute opening range from the 9:30 New York candle high and low, then go long when a candle breaks above the range and closes outside it; enter at the open of the next candle. The speaker also notes a cutoff of no new entries after the 12:00 candle and avoids ranges that are too small/
strategies.exit_summary: Place the stop loss at the bottom of the opening range and target 1.5:1 reward-to-risk.

strategies.name: opening_range_breakout_pullback_continuation
strategies.entry_summary: On a 5-minute chart, define the opening range using the first three 5-minute candles, wait for an initial upside breakout, then wait for price to pull back toward the range. A valid pullback candle breaks through the range but closes back above it, and the long entry is taken only after the next-cc3
strategies.exit_summary: Stop loss is placed at the bottom of the opening range; the speaker also mentions a compatible variant of placing the stop at the bottom of the pullback candle. Target is 1.5:1 reward-to-risk, with larger R targets later tested as variants.

variants.timeframe_note: 5-minute chart with opening range defined by first three 5-minute candles
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: enter on break of the most recent high after a pullback candle breaks below the range and closes back above it
variants.transcript_quote: Once I get this pullback candle, I don't enter immediately... I'm going to be waiting for a break of this most recent high.

variants.variant_label: same pullback-continuation skeleton with larger profit targets
variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: same confirmation entry after pullback and continuation
variants.transcript_quote: I reran the simulation and this time I tested take-profit ratios starting at 2 1/2 and going all the way up to 4 1/2

strategies.name: opening_range_breakout_pullback_top_of_range_stop_order
strategies.entry_summary: After an opening-range breakout, wait for price to pull back to the top of the opening range and use a stop order there to enter immediately on the bounce, instead of waiting for confirmation via a break of the prior high.
strategies.exit_summary: Stop loss remains at the bottom of the opening range and take profit is 1.5:1 reward-to-risk.

strategies.name: opening_range_breakout_pullback_midpoint_stop_order
strategies.entry_summary: After measuring the breakout from the top of the opening range, wait for a deeper pullback to the midpoint of the opening range and buy immediately with a stop order when price reaches that midpoint, without waiting for a break of a previous high.
strategies.exit_summary: Because entry is at the midpoint, the stop loss is smaller; the transcript frames the stop as tighter than prior versions while still using a 1.5:1 target as the stated test case.

result.enumeration_note: The video teaches four runnable long-entry skeletons with explicit stop/target mechanics: the original 15-minute ORB breakout, a pullback-confirmation continuation version, a top-of-range stop-order pullback entry, and a midpoint stop-order pullback entry; later mention of 'doing the opposite' momentum-focused breakout is not promoted because no concrete runnable exit is taught.
